text:
karim: Heads up — starting canary sweeps for NV driver/kernel combo to try and reduce Xid crashes. Rolling driver 535.86 -> 536.2 on a small subset of eu-west-1 GPU racks (g4/g5 pools). Looking for Xid spikes, ECC flips, and unexpected reboots. I'll push telemetry and a smoke script and post results live.

maya: Which exact nodes/labels are in the canary? rollback gates?

karim: subset: rack-34-[01-08], rack-36-[01-06], rack-42-[01-06]. Node label = canary=driver-536. Rollback criteria: Xid > 5 per host per hour OR ECC corrected > 10 in 1h OR > 2 host reboots in 24h. Start at ~10% capacity.

sam: Can we add an Xid_rate_per_gpu metric (sum(xid_count)/hours / gpus)? Also gate if driver logs include repeated 'RMX' or 'GPU HANG' substrings.

jing: I'll patch the alerts and add a Grafana rule. Proposed alert: sum(rate(nvidia_xid_total[5m])) by (node) > 0.1 -> infra-oncall. Adding runbook link.

oliver: Prefer host-level cordon then drain to avoid churn. Command to use: `kubectl cordon node-01 && kubectl drain node-01 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — also taint with gpu-canary=hold to stop new scheduling.

karim: Exact smoke test I'm running (quick):
```
# short heavy matrix multiply + check
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -c "import torch; a=__import__('torch').randn(4096,1024).cuda(); print(a.mm(a.t()).sum())"
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.total,utilization.gpu --format=csv
journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced --no-pager | tail -n 200
```

deploy-bot: deploy canary-driver-536 to rack-34-36-42: started by @karim

infra-oncall: If any node starts flapping, tag with repro=disabled and move to repair-pool.

maya: If we see kernel-specific regressions, we should fallback the kernel (eg. 6.1.12-1) before swapping drivers. Keep that path open.

karim: Will collect dmesg, nvidia logs, nv-hostengine traces and upload artifacts to s3://redwood-gpu-canary/1718203456/ — grabbing timestamps and core dumps if present.

sam: Add NVML traces and /var/log/nvidia/* tarball to the artifact list. Also include the output of `nvidia-smi -q` and dmesg | grep -i nvrm.

jing: Updated alert group: gpu_xid_alert -> added runbook https://go/repo/gpu-runbooks/xid-triage and paging policy.

deploy-bot: canary step1 finished: 4 nodes updated in rack-34; 10m elapsed; no critical alerts yet.

maya: Observed one corrected ECC event on rack-36 node-05 at 12:14 UTC. Counted it — below our threshold.

sam: We saw an Xid 31 on rack-36 node-07 around 12:22 UTC. Job resumed, but I'm opening a short incident note to capture the artifact.

karim: Force-cordoned node-07 and started drain. It has 1/8 GPUs showing GPU ECC flips + Xid. Thinking replacement of that card if it reproduces under stress.

oliver: Let's cordon + put node-07 into repair pool. Use internal tool: `nodectl replace-gpu --node node-07 --slot 1` after confirming physical slot. Also run GPU memtest.

infra-oncall: Marked node-07 for deep diagnostics and BIOS/firmware check (NVidia card firmware + system BMC). Running kernel and module version diff.

deploy-bot: canary step2 rolled to rack-42: 6 nodes. Alert gpu_xid_alert fired for node-07.

karim: Stopping further rollout. Rolling back driver on node-07 to 535.86 and collecting logs. Will pause full rollout until we correlate with kernel.

maya: Thanks. Can we reduce next batch size to 5% and expand telemetry windows to 2h before increasing batch? Also add per-GPU Xid thresholds rather than per-host only.

sam: Agreed. Also add check for repeated nv-hostengine restarts in the last 30m as a gating metric.

karim: Summary update: initial evidence points to a regression in driver 536.2 when combined with kernel 6.4.x on a small subset of hardware (certain g5 boards). Action items: rollback affected nodes, replace one flaky GPU, add kernel-driver compatibility matrix to CI, and extend canary observation windows. Follow-up doc: https://go/repo/eng/infra/gpu-driver-sweeps (I'll author a short postmortem with artifacts).

oliver: Good call to stop early. Once we have the nv-hostengine / dmesg diffs we can open a ticket with vendor to escalate a possible firmware interaction.

karim: tagging @infra-oncall @maya @sam for follow-ups. I'll post the postmortem and artifact link when ready.

infra-oncall: Acknowledged — keeping node-07 in repair. Will update when hardware tests complete.

karim: end of thread — will reconvene after hardware tests and kernel team review.
